subject: POC Workload Intake: burst windows, RPS profile, and acceptance timeline
messages:
From: Lucas Moreno <lucas@novamed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@novamed.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps from today's discovery — workload details attached

Kim — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can scope the POC: 

- Goal: evaluate Redwood for inference of our clinical triage assistant (summarization + routing). Success = >=95% availability at target latency and parity with our current model outputs on the provided eval set.
- High-level workload: mix of short queries (1-2 sentences) and long notes (200-1,200 tokens). We attached an initial sample payloads file and a short requirements spreadsheet.

Open items for Redwood:
1) Can you confirm what warm-up/run-in you recommend for kv-cache-heavy workloads?
2) We have a predictable morning burst (09:00–09:20 PT) where traffic spikes ~6x baseline for ~15 minutes. The rest of the day is steady at lower RPS.
3) What telemetry will you capture and share during the POC (p50/p95 latency, token cost breakdown, request-level traces)?

Asha and I can provide a more complete slice of payloads by EOD Friday if that helps. Attaching: nova_poc_requirements.xlsx, sample_payloads.jsonl

Thanks — Lucas
Senior Product Manager | NovaMed Health
[Attachment: nova_poc_requirements.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)]
[Attachment: sample_payloads.jsonl (jsonl, 120KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Moreno <lucas@novamed.com>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@novamed.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps from today's discovery — workload details attached

Lucas — great to catch up. Thanks for the summary and the attachments; they make scoping much easier. Replied inline + next steps below.

Inline answers:
1) Warm-up: for KV-cache heavy models we recommend a short warm-up for model shards plus a 10–15 minute synthetic ramp that exercises long-context tokens. For your morning burst (6x for ~15 minutes) we suggest one pre-warm window and enabling transient burst capacity on Dedicated (if you choose Dedicated) or policy-based burst on Hosted.
2) Telemetry: we will provide p50/p90/p95 latency, per-request token breakdown (input vs generated), GPU utilization, batching stats, and a per-request trace id you can map to your logs. We'll also surface failed-generation reasons.
3) Acceptance criteria template: availability >= 95% during burst windows, p95 latency <= 650ms for short queries (<=64 tokens), and model output score parity within an agreed threshold on your eval set (we'll wire up your eval suite).

Proposed POC timeline (draft):
- Day 0 (kickoff): exchange test creds, topology (VPC/whitelist) if needed, and finalize payload slice (owner: Lucas)
- Day 1–2: baseline runs + warm-up experiments (owner: Redwood - Karthik)
- Day 3: burst simulation and tuning (owner: Redwood + NovaMed ops)
- Day 4: eval run against your golden set + readout (owner: joint)
- Day 5: acceptance decision and next-step proposal

Ownership: Kimberly (sales) will coordinate logistics; Karthik (inference eng) will own the runbook and tuning. Ben (solutions) will help with sample payload ingestion and HubSpot activity.

Can you confirm Lucas/Asha: 1) an agreed sample window for the morning burst (date/time we should simulate) and 2) whether we can use the sample_payloads.jsonl as-is or you will send a filtered subset? Once confirmed we can lock the exact POC start date.

I'll also add a short checklist we can iterate on.

—Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Moreno <lucas@novamed.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps from today's discovery — workload details attached

Lucas — quick technical note from infra before we schedule the runs. Thanks for the sample payloads, that helps. A couple of items we'd like to codify for the POC harness: 

- RPS / concurrency: Please provide a small matrix example: baseline RPS, peak RPS during burst, concurrent open connections expected. Example format we accept: {baseline: 12 rps, peak: 72 rps, concurrency: 18}.
- Token distribution: a histogram or buckets would be ideal (e.g., 50% <=64 tokens, 35% 65–300, 15% >300–1200). This tells us batching shapes and memory profile.
- Burst shape: is the morning spike a sharp 1–2 minute ramp or a more gradual 10–15 minute sustained increase? That affects our pre-warm recommendation.
- Warm cache strategy: we will run a controlled pre-warm set that seeds the KV/cache and then run a 15-minute synthetic replay of long contexts. If you want to avoid synthetic replay on production data, we can do the warm using a representative synthetic set.

For telemetry hooks: we'll create a shared dashboard with traces and also attach a zip of request-level logs at the end of each run (redacted for PHI). If you need HIPA A-level controls during the POC, let us know and we will enable stricter redaction steps.

If you can drop the small RPS/token matrix and a preferred date window for simulation (we're flexible next week), we will schedule a 60–90 minute run and capture p95/p99, success-rate, and cost-per-1000 tokens.

Cheers,
Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Lucas Moreno <lucas@novamed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@novamed.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T14:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps from today's discovery — workload details attached

Thanks — quick answers and sample matrix below. We'll aim to start the POC next Tuesday (2027-04-12) morning window if that works.

Attached small matrix (inline):
- Baseline: 15 RPS
- Peak (morning burst): 90 RPS sustained for ~15 minutes (09:00–09:15 PT)
- Concurrency: expected 20 concurrent open requests during peak (most are short queries)

Token distribution (approx):
- 55% <= 64 tokens
- 30% 65–300 tokens
- 15% 301–1,200 tokens

Burst shape: sustained 15-minute plateau with 2–3 short micro-spikes inside it (1–2 minute 1.5x spikes).

Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Availability >= 95% during the burst window
- p95 latency <= 650ms for <=64 token queries; p95 <= 1,200ms for 301–1,200 token requests
- Output parity: F1 >= 0.88 on your eval run vs our golden set (we'll provide scoring scripts)

We will use the provided sample_payloads.jsonl as-is for the first run; we can provide a filtered smaller file if you prefer a shorter smoke test. 

Please confirm the 4/12 start date or suggest another. We'll get the final golden set to you by EOD Monday.

–Lucas
Senior Product Manager | NovaMed Health
[Attachment: sample_payloads.jsonl (jsonl, 120KB)]
